newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends up on technical bounce, commercials.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends up on technical bounce, commercials.

text.p: Commercial buying and a technical bounce boosted CBOT corn futures to a higher close, traders said.
"There's commercial buying with Cargill in there," a trader said.

Cargill Inc, Farmers Commodities Corp and Tenco Inc each bought one million bushels of December, traders said. Griffin Trading sold three million bushels of March and ADM Investor Services sold 2.5 million December, they said.
Volume was thin which allowed the relatively small amounts of commercial demand to move prices higher, the traders said.
The market still was digesting Friday's USDA crop report.

The government's October crop report showed 1996 U.S. corn production at 9.012 billion bushels, above trade expectations for 8.951 billion. Corn futures dropped Friday but found scant selling interest in early dealings Monday. Also corn recently was hit hard and due for a technical correction.
New crop December Friday dropped to a low of $2.83 per bushel, a 27 percent loss in value from the contract's high of $3.89 which was set July 12.
Corn closed one to 3-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with December up 2-3/4 at $2.86-1/2.
December's nine day relative strength index (RSI) closed at 28.172 points, above the commonly perceived very oversold point of 20 yet below the oversold level of 30.

The session low for December was $2.82-1/4 per bushel, which was right on the first chart support level of $2.82-1/4. The first resistance level was pegged by technicians at $285-1/2 and the second resistance was at $2.89.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 60,000 contracts, down from 77,446 Friday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options, The Chicago Corp bought 1,500 March $2.80 puts at 6-1/2 to seven cents, sold 600 March $3.40 puts at 49-1/2 to 50 cents and Tenco Inc sold 500 March $2.70 puts at four cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 27,000 contracts, down from 41,607 Friday.
